extracted.intended_audience: investor relations and corporate communications professionals; researchers of voluntary disclosure and financial communications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing earnings/financial press releases so they integrate effectively with accompanying conference calls and the broader voluntary-disclosure ecosystem to influence analyst forecasts and media pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference calls increase analysts' forecast accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference calls increase analysts' forecast accuracy — implying the call adds information beyond the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use presence and substance of a conference call as a metric of whether the firm's disclosure system will materially improve analysts' forecasts; a release alone may not supply the incremental information analysts get from calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference calls reduce forecast dispersion
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference calls reduce forecast dispersion — analyst convergence increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful call should narrow analyst disagreement; measure disclosure effectiveness not only by mean forecast change but by dispersion among analysts after the call/release pair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects are larger for firms with higher analyst following
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects are larger for firms with higher analyst following — a size/coverage interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor disclosure strategy to analyst coverage: the incremental value of calls and richer release content is greater for firms with more analysts; small-cap firms with sparse coverage may rely more on the release alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release / conference-call alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should cover all material headline items; the call expands narrative and Q&A. If the call introduces material new information not in the release, the release was incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure material facts and headline numbers are present in the release; reserve the call for elaboration, interpretation, and Q&A rather than primary disclosure of material new information (which could create regulatory exposure and confuse downstream audiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-call release timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Release distribution must precede the call by enough time that participants can read it (typically 30+ minutes); release-after-call is a Reg FD violation if any material content varies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule distribution so attendees have reasonable time to read the release before the call (authors note ~30+ minutes); never post material changes after a call in a way that privileges informed participants and risks Fair Disclosure violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q&A-anticipation hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Include in the release the data and context that analysts will ask about anyway. This signals preparation and converts well into call time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate likely analyst questions and provide the key data/context in the release (not just in prepared remarks) so the call can focus on clarification and deeper discussion rather than basic disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking guidance placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative guidance should appear in the press release proper (with safe-harbor language), not only in the call. Per Bowen et al., guidance affects analyst forecasts measurably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place substantive guidance (numbers, ranges) in the release and include appropriate safe-harbor/forward-looking statements language; relying on the call alone to convey guidance reduces its reach and may lower pickup-worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation table
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro-forma to GAAP reconciliations belong in the release, not in the call deck — analysts demand the audit trail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish reconciliations and bridge tables within the release so analysts and modelers have the audit trail; withholding reconciliations to the call deck inconveniences analysts and undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-script consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepared remarks should not contradict the release; deviations are flagged by analysts as either error or strategic shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency between the written release and scripted remarks; any necessary narrative divergence should be anticipated and explained, because contradictions are interpreted negatively by sophisticated audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q&A transcript availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Same-day transcript posting expands the release's downstream reach to analysts and journalists who could not join live.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post an accurate transcript of the Q&A promptly (same day) so those who missed the call receive equivalent information; timely transcripts increase the effective distribution of the call's informational content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-channel coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases should anticipate that some analysts read only the release (small-cap coverage), some attend only the call (large-cap), some read only the transcript. Each channel should carry the core message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft the core message so it is present across release, live call, and transcript. Recognize heterogeneous consumption patterns and avoid channel-specific materiality that leaves parts of the audience uninformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness: call/release pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: For pickup-worthy financial releases, the appropriate question is whether the call/release pair together maximize analyst (and downstream journalist) forecast accuracy, not whether the release alone gets reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate press releases in the context of the surrounding disclosure ecosystem; a release without an accompanying call often under-delivers to sophisticated users and may be demoted in pickup decisions. Plan release and call jointly to maximize informational impact.
